instruction: Add a keyword-only monotonic=False parameter to more_itertools.extract(iterable, indices). With monotonic=True the indices are read lazily, one at a time, so they may be infinite, but they must be non-decreasing; the iterable is consumed only as far as the index being produced. For example, with collatz = more_itertools.iterate(lambda x: 3 * x + 1 if x % 2 else x // 2, 42) and indices = itertools.count(0, 2), taking three values gives [42, 64, 16], after which next(collatz) is 8 and next(indices) is 6. A repeated index yields the same value again. A negative index, or an index smaller than the one before it, raises ValueError; an index beyond the end of the iterable raises IndexError, each when that index is reached. Without monotonic, extract behaves as before (indices read eagerly and in any order).
